events.title: Harold II defeats Harald Hardrada at Stamford Bridge
events.description: King Harold of England surprised and destroyed the Norwegian army near York, killing Harald Hardrada and Tostig. Three days later William of Normandy landed in the south, forcing Harold to march back.
events.html: King Harold of England surprised and destroyed the Norwegian army near York, killing Harald Hardrada and Tostig. Three days later William of Normandy landed in the south, forcing Harold to march back.

events.title: Henry III and Alexander II agree the Treaty of York
events.description: At York, Henry III of England and Alexander II of Scotland agreed that Northumberland, Cumberland and Westmorland were subject to English sovereignty. The treaty fixed the Anglo-Scottish border almost as it remains, ending Scottish attempts to extend the frontier south.
events.html: At York, Henry III of England and Alexander II of Scotland agreed that Northumberland, Cumberland and Westmorland were subject to English sovereignty. The treaty fixed the Anglo-Scottish border almost as it remains, ending Scottish attempts to extend the frontier south.

events.title: Bayezid I routs Sigismund's crusaders at Nicopolis
events.description: On the lower Danube, the Ottoman sultan Bayezid I routed a crusading army led by King Sigismund of Hungary. The defeat ended the last large-scale joint crusade of medieval Europe and left the Ottomans firmly in control of Bulgaria.
events.html: On the lower Danube, the Ottoman sultan Bayezid I routed a crusading army led by King Sigismund of Hungary. The defeat ended the last large-scale joint crusade of medieval Europe and left the Ottomans firmly in control of Bulgaria.

events.title: Balboa becomes the first European to see the Pacific from the Americas
events.description: Vasco Núñez de Balboa climbed a peak on the Isthmus of Panama and sighted the 'South Sea'. Days later he waded into the water and claimed it and all its shores for Castile.
events.html: Vasco Núñez de Balboa climbed a peak on the Isthmus of Panama and sighted the 'South Sea'. Days later he waded into the water and claimed it and all its shores for Castile.

events.title: The Peace of Augsburg is signed
events.description: Agreed between Emperor Charles V's government and the Lutheran princes, the treaty let each ruler in the Holy Roman Empire choose Lutheranism or Catholicism as his state's official confession. Calvinism was not allowed until the Peace of Westphalia.
events.html: Agreed between Emperor Charles V's government and the Lutheran princes, the treaty let each ruler in the Holy Roman Empire choose Lutheranism or Catholicism as his state's official confession. Calvinism was not allowed until the Peace of Westphalia.

events.title: The English Parliament accepts the Solemn League and Covenant
events.description: The English Parliament and the Westminster Assembly accepted the Solemn League and Covenant with the Scottish Covenanters, already approved by the Church of Scotland. It promised religious reforms in England and Ireland in exchange for Scottish troops against King Charles I.
events.html: The English Parliament and the Westminster Assembly accepted the Solemn League and Covenant with the Scottish Covenanters, already approved by the Church of Scotland. It promised religious reforms in England and Ireland in exchange for Scottish troops against King Charles I.

events.title: Ethan Allen fails to capture Montreal at Longue-Pointe
events.description: Ethan Allen and a small force of American and Quebec militia failed in an attempt to capture Montreal from the British. Major John Brown, who Allen claimed was to bring reinforcements, did not appear, leaving them isolated across the St Lawrence.
events.html: Ethan Allen and a small force of American and Quebec militia failed in an attempt to capture Montreal from the British. Major John Brown, who Allen claimed was to bring reinforcements, did not appear, leaving them isolated across the St Lawrence.

events.title: Congress proposes the amendments that become the Bill of Rights
events.description: The First Congress sent twelve proposed amendments to the states. Ten were ratified in 1791 as the Bill of Rights, protecting freedoms of speech, religion, press and assembly.
events.html: The First Congress sent twelve proposed amendments to the states. Ten were ratified in 1791 as the Bill of Rights, protecting freedoms of speech, religion, press and assembly.

events.title: Sonny Liston knocks out Floyd Patterson to win the world title
events.description: Sonny Liston took the world heavyweight title in Chicago by knocking out Floyd Patterson in 2 minutes 6 seconds of the first round. He lost the title to Cassius Clay in 1964.
events.html: Sonny Liston took the world heavyweight title in Chicago by knocking out Floyd Patterson in 2 minutes 6 seconds of the first round. He lost the title to Cassius Clay in 1964.
